post.description:
Remove the cached answers of a tenant, or of one of its aliases.

Redis and PostgreSQL share no transaction, so the action is recorded right
after the answers are removed. If PostgreSQL fails in between, the answers
are gone, the action is missing from the history and the request gets 503.
Create a gateway API key for a tenant, and the tenant if needed.
Revoke a gateway API key. Gateways refuse it once their key cache expires (60 s).

get.description:
Describe the operator signed in with the session of the request.

Allowed during a forced password change: the dashboard reads it to know.

put.description: Choose the language of the dashboard. No password needed: it is only a preference.

Change one's own password. Allowed, and needed, during a forced password change.

The other sessions of the operator are closed; this one stays open.

get.description: Return every operator account, enabled or not.

post.description: Create an operator account. Its owner must change the password at the first sign-in.

Disable an operator account and close all its sessions at once.

One cannot disable oneself, nor the last enabled account.
Enable an operator account again: it can sign in with its password.

Give another operator a new password, and close all their sessions at once.

They must change it at the next sign-in. To change one's own password, use
`PUT /admin/v1/me/password` instead.

Open a session with a username and a password.

A wrong password, an unknown username, a disabled account and a locked
account all get the same answer, so the answer never tells which usernames exist.
